title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Monday (Tone Adam)
text:
Thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand sing and give praise to our Lord Jesus. Everything that says that the Lord is Jesus is a sword at hand to scatter the enemy. For thou truly art very greatly exalted beyond the heavens and above the earth. For all the just who are pleasing to God meditate in all thy law.

God is placed before them always, his holy name is always in their mouths.

Greatly exalted is thy kindness, thou doer of righteous things, O Lord Jesus.

God is Emmanuel, the true food, the tree of life, the deathless.

Collect within me all forms of speech that I may laud and glorify the Lord Jesus.

Jesus is our God, Jesus is our Lord, Jesus is the hope of Christians.

Little by little we reach thy remembrance and glorify thy name, O Lord Jesus.

Every distraction that exists may we lay aside, that we may purge our hearts with the name of the Lord Jesus.

May thy name, O Lord, be within us, that it may enlighten us in our inner man.

For who amongst the gods is like unto thee, O Lord? Thou art the true god who doest wonders.

Blessed art thou in truth, O Lord Jesus, with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit.

A sweet savour very greatly famous is thy holy name, O Lord Jesus.

O true lamb of God the Father, have mercy on us in thy kingdom.

For the mouth of thy Father which bears witness to thee that "thou art my son, to-day have I begotten thee".

They glorify thee, the cherubim and seraphim; they cannot look upon thee.

We behold thee, the lamb, upon the place of sacrifice; we take of thy body and thy sacred blood.

Every hymn which is in all the law, there is nothing else therein but similitudes of thee.

This is the true stone most precious, which the merchant sold his possessions and bought.

Bestow upon us now this stone, that it may illuminate us in the inner man.

Consolation of our souls, freshness of our hearts is thy holy name, O Lord Jesus.

O pitiful and merciful, of great pity, O Lord Jesus.

The cherubim wave their wings; they sing and give praise, O Lord Jesus.

The sun will set and the moon in time; but thou, thou art, thy years do not fail.

In the providence of thy goodness thou dost bend the heavens, thou dost descend upon us.

As the true physician who gives healing thou dost cure all our diseases.

Look upon me, O Lord Jesus, with the pitying eye of thy goodness.

Plant within us an upright heart that we may bless thee, O Lord Jesus.

I pray to thee, Lord Jesus, have mercy on us in thy kingdom.

Moreover when we may give ourselves to prayer, let us bless the name of the Lord Jesus. For I will praise thee, O Lord Jesus, through thy name, for I have trusted in thee. Let us laud thee with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit, for thou didst rise and save us.

title: Alternative Psali for Monday
text:
O come ye daily, all ye orthodox, in order that we may praise Mary the Virgin.

Every creature lauds the pure one, the full of glory, Mary the Virgin.

For she is exalted above the angels and the hosts on high, Mary the Virgin.

David the psalmist spoke well of her glory, as "the pure dove", Mary the Virgin.

On account of the Mother of God, the pure maiden, Mary the Virgin, purge us, O Lord Christ.

The seven angels and powers and thrones give praise in hymns to Mary the Virgin.

Fortunately did she bear our Lord Jesus Christ, the Word of God, Mary the Virgin.

To thee be glory and honour, O Son of God, and thy Queen Mother, Mary the Virgin.

Jesus Christ our God took bodily form from the Mother of God, Mary the Virgin.

According to thy greatness, have mercy on us, O good One, on account of thy maiden mother, Mary the Virgin.

The faithful people utter hymns to thee, O pure censer, Mary the Virgin.

Give to us thy peace, save us in temptations, heal our infirmities, Mary the Virgin.

Have mercy upon us, remove thy anger from us, O Son of God, for the sake of the blessed Mary the Virgin.

Blessed One, save us from temptations, for the sake of the prayers over us of Mary the Virgin.

Great is her glory above the angels, daughter of David the King, Mary the Virgin.

Crown of our praise, we are amongst the faithful, O mother of all who live, Mary the Virgin.

Rejoice ye faithful and exult in the Lord, on account of the Mother of God, Mary the Virgin.

Bless the Lord our God, say psalms at the birth of the Mother of God, Mary the Virgin.

Greatly art thou exalted above things immaterial, O Mother of the King of Glory, Mary the Virgin.

Son of God, give to us our perfection as Christians, and save us for the name of Mary the Virgin.

O God, exalt the horn of Christians, through the prayers of our Lord, Mary the Virgin.

Hail, throne of Jesus Christ; hail paradise, Mary the Virgin.

Souls give glory with the just, on account of the Queen, Mary the Virgin.

O Lord, remember me with thy servant Nicodemus, for the sake of the new heaven, Mary the Virgin.

title: The Monday Theotokia (Tone Adam)
text:
I. When Adam became of contrite heart the Lord vouchsafed to restore him, as at first. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

II. Eve, whom the serpent deceived, received sentence from the Lord: "In multiplying there should be multiplied afflictions of heart and groanings." The Lord took pity because of his love for men: he made good will again and set her free. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

III. Jesus Christ, the Word, who took flesh, came and dwelt among us; we saw his glory: "Like the glory of the only Son of the Father he vouchsafed to save us." He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

IV. With prophetic eyes did Esaias see the mystery of Emmanuel. He the great prophet therefore cried and said: "A child is born to us, a son is given to us: there is authority placed upon his shoulders. God, the powerful, the almighty, and the angel of great counsel." He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

V. Rejoice and exult, O race of men, that God did so love the world: "That he gave his beloved son, so that believers in him might live for ever." For he descended by reason of his mercy, and extended to us an outstretched arm. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

VI. He who has been is he who will be; he who came comes again. Jesus Christ the Word made flesh, without change of substance, was perfect man. He does not destroy or disturb or divide in any way as concerns the unity. But is the same nature, the same substance, the same person, that is God the Word. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

VII. Hail Bethlehem, city of the prophets, who within thee didst bear Christ the second Adam: that he might restore Adam the first man from the earth to Paradise, and make void the sentence of death: "Thou Adam art earth and shalt return to earth." "For where sin was abundant, there much more abounded the grace of Christ." He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

VIII. Let every soul rejoice and sing, in chorus with the angels, a song to the king Christ. They cry aloud and say: "Glory to God in the highest, and peace upon earth, and good will amongst men." For he has broken down the wall of partition; he has abolished the fullness of enmity. He has blotted out the handwriting of condemnation on Adam and Eve; he has made them free. He who was born to us in the city of David according to the word of the angel is our Saviour Christ. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

IX. God is light, he is in the light; angels of light sing hymns to him. The light was born of Mary: Elisabeth conceived the precursor. The Holy Spirit stirred in David: "Arise and sing that the light has arisen." David arose, the holy singer, he took his harp of spiritual nature. He hasted to the church, the house of the angels; he sung and hymned the Holy Trinity. In thy light, O Lord, do we see light; may thy loving-kindness continue to those who know thee. The true light which enlightens every man coming into the world. Thou didst come into the world through thy love for men; all creation did rejoice at thy coming. Thou didst save Adam from error; thou didst liberate Eve from the sorrow of death. Thou didst give us the spirit of adoption; we sing and bless thee with thy angels. He took bodily form from the Virgin, without the seed of man, that he might save us.

title: The Monday Theotokia — Crown
text: Indeed my tongue, unworthy and sinful, does not venture to speak to the glory of Mary. For Adam our father, the first created at the hands of the God, the Creator, through the advice of Eve, our first mother, did Adam eat of the fruit of the tree. There came upon our race and all creation the punishment of death and destruction. Through Mary, the Mother of God, Adam was restored again as he was at first. Behold, the kings, mighty David and Solomon, make hymns to her and honour her. David the prophet spoke to her honour, he called her the city of God. Solomon also the Ecclesiast in the Song of Songs spoke thus of her: "My sister, my beloved, she that is perfect; the smell of her clothing is a sweet savour." All ye virgins desire chastity, that ye may be daughters of the holy Mary. For indeed through her did the race of women find boldness before the Lord.

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Tuesday (Tone Adam)
text:
Come to us every day, O Lord Jesus; give light to us in thy exalted deity. Send upon us the great grace of thy Holy Spirit the Paraclete. That we may speak some small things of praise on account of thy name holy and blessed. This has caused glory in the mouths of thy saints, thy holy ones who are upon earth: "Who wandered forth in the mountain deserts in hunger and thirst and cold and fasting": who were oppressed and suffered affliction, according to the sayings of Paul the Apostle.

But thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, saves them in all afflictions.

Thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, is of great glory in all tribulation.

It was to them true nourishment, feeding their souls and bodies together.

It was to them a fountain of the water of life, sweet in their throat more than honey.

They declared it with a glad heart; also their flesh declared it forth.

They related it until their mind uplifted the harp, and so also their heart might exalt him on high.

Moreover when we assemble for prayer let us bless the name of the Lord Jesus. For I will bless thee, O Lord Jesus, and render thanks to thy name, for I have trusted in thee. So may we praise thee with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit, for thou didst rise and save us.

title: Alternative Psali for Tuesday
text:
Save me, O Lord; give me penitence, that we may say thus, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Help our infirmity, purge away our sins, that we may sing to thee a thousand times, "Hail to thee, Mary."

For thou art our Lord, the sinless Word; we sing to thee our Lord, "Hail to thee, Mary."

The righteous one has conceived the sinless Christ; we glorify and exalt thee, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Have mercy on us through the intercessions of thy mother Mary, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Greatly uplifted are the melodies to the Mother of the King of Glory, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Behold, we the faithful in doxologies duly praise thee, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Send thy might and blessing to thy community, O King of Glory, "Hail to thee, Mary."

May Jesus Christ our God give power for she bare him as God, "Hail to thee, Mary."

According to the greatness of the multitude of thy potencies, O Word of God, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Every race lauds thee in songs, O Creator, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Give to us thy peace and thy election with the mother of light, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Have mercy on us, and save us from evils and oppressions, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Blessed art thou, O Christ; fill us with thy wisdom for the sake of the Mother of God, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Glory to thee, O God, amongst thy community; we honour the Mother of God, "Hail to thee, Mary."

O Lord, drive away the enemies of the church, tribulation and distress; "Hail to thee, Mary."

Watch over us, O Christ; protect us in our goings, and griefs and enmities; "Hail to thee, Mary."

Hear us in our trials, purge from us our sins through intercession; "Hail to thee, Mary."

We praise and laud thee in psalms, the Beginning and Endless One, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Son of God, bless thy inheritance and guard them, "Hail to thee, Mary."

To thee be power and thanksgiving, O Christ, lover of men, "Hail to thee, Mary."

Hail Virgin, hail holy one, hail pure one, "Hail to thee, Mary."

The souls that thou hast taken give them safety in thy kingdom, "Hail to thee, Mary."

O Lord Christ give me safety, the servant Nicodemus, "Hail to thee, Mary."

title: The Tuesday Theotokia (Tone Adam)
text:
I. The crown of our praise, the beginning of our salvation, and the confirmation of our redemption is Mary the Virgin. She bare to us God the Word, who became man for our salvation. After he became man he was still God, therefore she who bare him remains a virgin. Exalted is the wonder of her virginity; her child-bearing also is beyond speech. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

II. Great is the glory of the perfect virginity of Mary the Virgin. Thou art full of grace, the Lord is with thee: thou art the ladder which Jacob saw. Set up upon earth it reached towards heaven; there were the angels going upon it. Thou art the tree which Moses saw, filled with fire and not consumed. That was the Son of God who was in thy womb; the fire of his Deity did not consume thy body. Thou art the field which was not sown; it brought forth living fruit. Thou art the treasure which Joseph gathered; he acquired the pearl whose price was great. Our Saviour Jesus was found in thy womb; thou didst bear him into the world that he might save us. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

III. Hail, Mother of God, joy of the angels; hail, holy one, preached of the prophets. Hail, thou who hast obtained grace, the Lord is with thee; hail, exalted above the angels, rejoicing of the world. Hail, thou who didst bear the maker of everything; hail, thou who wast worthy to be called the Mother of the Christ. Hail, thou who didst give salvation to Adam and Eve; hail, thou who didst procure nourishment for every creature. Hail, holy one, mother of all who live; thee do we implore to intercede for us. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

IV. Whenever one regards thee, O holy Virgin and Mother of God, and the mystery which was most wonderful that was in thee for our salvation; he will not be silent because of its unspeakable character; he will stir us up to sing hymns: on account of the greatness of that miracle, that it might be beneficial in various ways. For the living word of God the Father, who came under the law on Mount Sinai. He covered the mountain top with darkness and gloom and storm and tempest; by the sound of trumpetings he taught in fear those who came there. He stood down upon it, the reasonable mountain, in gentleness; and again in love he took flesh for men in her, without change of substance, a reasonable body, consubstantial with us, perfectly complete, at one with his mother, a soul supernal. He remained God continuously, and became perfect man; in order that he might remove the transgression of Adam and save him who was lost; that he might be a citizen of heaven above, and be restored as at the first through his great mercy. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

V. The honour of the Virgin is indescribable, for God has chosen her; he came and was in her. He who was in the light unapproachable remained in her womb nine months. The invisible and unlimited did Mary conceive and remain a virgin. For this is the stone which Daniel saw, that was cut out from the mountain. The hand of man did not touch it, that is the Word which is from the Father. He came and took flesh of the Virgin, without seed of man, that he might save us. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

VI. It was the branch of purification and the establishment of the orthodox Faith of our holy fathers, O holy and sacred virgin. She conceived for us God the Word; our Saviour Jesus came and saved us. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

VII. She is the mother of the light, the pure mother of God, that was for the Word unconfined. After she bare him she remained still a virgin; with songs and praises we exalt her. For he, in his desire with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit, came and saved us.

title: The Tuesday Theotokia — Crown
text: There is no tongue of flesh competent to praise thee, O holy Virgin, and Mother of God. For thou wast the royal throne where he was placed between the cherubim. In what manner shall we felicitate thee? for thou didst bear into nature the spiritual one who is its superior. Thy name is remembered in every generation, O pure dove and mother of Christ. Rejoice Mary, Maiden and Mother, for to him who was in thy breast do the angels sing hymns, and the cherubim rightly praise him, and the seraphim without cessation. They shelter him with their wings, for this is the King of Glory, who takes away the sins of the world according to his great mercy. We ourselves pray that we may obtain mercy through thy intercessions to him the Lover of men.

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Wednesday
text:
Let them rejoice and be glad, those who seek after the Lord, those who continue always in meditation on his holy name. Those are the trees concerning whom the psalmist David said that they are planted by springs of water and give forth perfect fruit. The spring of water is our Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ; they who continue with him their soul shall live. The holy scriptures teach us of the rivers of God, that we may attain mercy within the creation he has made.

And again that love will never pass away, according to the saying of the wise Apostle Paul. The love of which he spoke, that holy Apostle, that is the saving name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Let us love the saving name of our Lord Jesus Christ that we may be merciful one to another, and so that we may fulfil all the law.

Through mercy Abraham had good will, wherefore God dwelt with him and his holy angels. Through mercy the just Lot was saved from the severe judgement which came upon Sodom. Through mercy Cornelius was found worthy to receive baptism at the hands of our father Peter. For behold we are at last in the judgement of the world; there is no other one from whom we may find mercy.

That is the precious stone, the pearl greatly desired, the name sweet and full of glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. Whenever we adhere to him in our inner man he will give to us richly so that we may give to one another. The judgements of this world will pass through searchings, but the salvation of our souls is in the meditation of his holy name.

Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls. Glory be to Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and for all ages. Amen.

title: Alternative Psali for Wednesday
text:
I have trusted in thee, O God; pardon me, O Lord Jesus, through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Mary the pure dove.

Every being upon earth praises the pure one, and all the hosts of heaven utter blessings. For thou art the Mother of God, and gate of the East, and second tabernacle, Mother of Christ Adonai.

David declared of her, "Glorious things are said of thee, O thou city of God," for Christ arose therein. Through Mary the Virgin were restored to Paradise Adam and the ancient fathers and prophets and righteous.

The seven hosts in heaven glorify the Queen, "The Father looked down from heaven and found none like thee."

Behold, in truth thou art exalted above the heavens and dominions, for all the kings of the earth walk in thy light. This is the cloud of light which came upon the King of Glory, for the Father formed her, the Holy Ghost came upon her.

Jesus, the son of the Most High, loved the Virgin, and the power of the Most High overshadowed thee, O Mary. For this is the greeting he sent from heaven, "Hail, thou full of grace, pure one, God is with thee." Moreover he spoke in joy and rejoicing, "Behold, thou shalt conceive and bear Emmanuel."

Mary the true spouse, Mary the saving of our race, Mary the true ladder which Jacob saw. Thou art the reasonable Paradise of Christ, with the root of the just, Mother of God the Word.

Rightly do the orthodox give praise in hymns: "Hail, throne of Christ, the Saviour of the world."

Joy of virginity and spiritual pain, paradoxical wonder according to the prophetic voices. Blessed is the child-bearing of Mary the Virgin, a wise maiden and blessed, a vessel of pure gold.

Rejoice, O true spouse, O true city of Sion, Mary the true Queen, Mother of the King of Ages. Hear us in our troubles and save us from our enemies, O Jesus Christ the only-begotten, and send forth good counsel.

Thou dost excel the cherubim, and dominions, and thrones; more holy than the seraphim, O Mary, Mother of Christ.

Behold Ezekiel said, "I saw a gate towards the east closed with a wonderful seal." Thou art the gate and the temple. God who rests amidst his saints was in her, she conceived him, as God he was seen.

Hail temple of God, Mother of Christ the Messiah, the unlimited Son of God, the One of the Trinity. Every soul that is in glory is in Paradise; Mary is the Mother of the King of Glory, Jesus Christ the Word.

O thou whom the Virgin conceived as God truly good, I am the least of men; place me amongst the faithful. Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls.

title: The Wednesday Theotokia
text:
I. All the hosts of heaven utter benedictions, for she is the second heaven which was upon earth. The gate of the east is Mary the Virgin, the holy spouse of the pure bridegroom. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

II. "Glorious things are said of thee, O thou city of God, for thou art the dwelling of all those who rejoice therein." All the kings of the earth go in thy glory and the nations in thy rising, O Mary, mother of God. All generations call her blessed; let us adore him who was begotten, let us the more exalt him. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

III. Thou art the glorious cloud which signified to us the rainfall of the coming of the only-begotten. The Father fashioned her, the Holy Spirit came upon her, the power of the Most High overshadowed Mary, so that she conceived the true Word, the Son of the Father, who endureth for ever, who came and saved us from our sins. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

IV. Great is the honour that thou, O Gabriel the angel, didst call her worthy; thou messenger of good, thy presence did spread joy. Thou didst signify to us the begetting of God who came to us; thou didst bring good tidings to Mary, the virgin undefiled. "Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee, for thou shalt find grace; the Holy Spirit shall come upon thee: the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee, O Mary, wherefore thou shalt conceive the Holy One, the Saviour of all the world." The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

V. A virgin bearing which calls our tongue daily to celebrate Mary the mother of God. Wherefore there was born to us in the city of David our Saviour Jesus and Christ the Lord. O come all ye people, let us bless her, for she was a mother and virgin together. Hail, O virgin, thou holy and undefiled, in whom the word of the Father came and took flesh. Hail, O perfect one, unspotted and elect, of true and perfect virginity. Hail reasonable paradise of Christ who was the second Adam for the sake of Adam the first man. Hail workshop of undivided unity of natures brought together at one time without confusion. Hail bridal chamber adorned in various ways for the true bridegroom who was joined to humanity. Hail spiritual bush of nature whom the fire of the Deity did not consume. Hail maiden and mother, virgin and heaven, who didst bear in bodily form him who is between the cherubim. In these things we exalt thee and sing with the holy angels; in gladness we say, "Glory to God in the highest, and peace upon earth and good will to men," for he made good will in her, he to whom is glory for ever. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

VI. Great is the glory of Mary above all the saints, for she gave nourishment to God the Word. Him before whom the angels fear did Mary the Virgin bear in her womb. Higher than the cherubim, holier than the seraphim, for she was the temple of One of the Trinity. She is Jerusalem, the city of our God; the gladness of all the saints is therein. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

VII. "Galilee of the Gentiles, which walked in darkness and the shadow of death, upon it has come a great light." God who dwells amongst his saints took flesh in the Virgin, thus bringing salvation. Come, behold and wonder, sing and rejoice with joy at this mystery which has been made manifest to us. For the fleshless has taken flesh and the Word is incarnate, the one without beginning commences life, the timeless enters time. The incomprehensible is comprehended, the unseen is seen, the Son of the Living God becomes Son of Man in truth. Jesus Christ yesterday and to-day he is, he is for ever; in the dispensation of unity let us praise and glorify her. The Father looked down from heaven, he found none like her, he sent his only-begotten Son who took flesh in her.

title: The Wednesday Theotokia — Crown
text: Ezekiel the prophet cried and bore witness, "I saw a door in the east; it was closed with a wonderful seal." No one enters therein except the Lord of Hosts; he has entered and come forth; it stands firm and is closed thus. For the door is the virgin who bare our Saviour, and after she conceived him remained still a virgin. Blessed is thy fruit, O thou who broughtest God into the world, that he might save us from the hands of the hateful tyrant. Perfect is thy favour, O thou who didst acquire every grace, before the King of Glory the true God. Thou art worthy of all honour beyond every creature that is on earth, for the Word of the Father came and took flesh in thee, and dwelt with men as man-loving and merciful, that he might save our souls through his holy advent. We pray thee be mindful, O faithful mediator, before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he take away our sins.

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Thursday (Tone Batos)
text:
Moreover, ye well-beloved, let us cast from us the lusts of our heart which entice us to sin. Let us praise the mighty name of our Lord Jesus Christ; with great unworthiness let us cry aloud and say:

O Lord Jesus Christ, begotten of the Father from all eternity, have mercy on us according to thy great mercy.

O Lord Jesus Christ, whom the Virgin bore in Bethlehem of Judah, save us and have mercy on us.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who wast baptized in the Jordan, cleanse our souls from the stain of sin.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who didst fast for us forty days and forty nights to save us from our sins.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who wast suspended on the cross and didst beat down Satan beneath our feet.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who wast buried in a sepulchre and didst overcome before us the sharpness of death.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who didst rise from the dead and ascend to the heavens and raise us by thy power.

O Lord Jesus Christ, who wilt come at thy second advent, deal with us in loving mercy at thy judgement seat which comes suddenly.

That is with favour to me with the good will of the Father and the Holy Spirit: thou didst come and save us. Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls.

title: Alternative Psali for Thursday
text:
I will begin, O beloved of God, Jesus Christ; let us praise the Mother of God, Mary the daughter of the just.

Everything praises thee, O Mary, Mother of Christ, the true bush which was in the desert.

For Moses the chief prophet saw the bush; the fire was filling it, yet its foliage did not burn.

David signified her thus: "Wings of a dove are adorned with feathers of silver and her back with yellow gold." "They bring to the king virgins that are her company, she with all her wonders into the temple of the Lord."

Great are thy melodies, the praise of all virgins, Mary the sacred and holy who is clothed with purity.

Behold, our first father Adam has recovered Paradise, Noe and our father Abraham, through Mary the Virgin.

She heard the voice of Gabriel the Angel; "Hail, the Lord is with thee, O thou pure bride."

Behold, she has conceived and borne a son, the Son of God Most High, and the prophets speak of her.

As said the Apostle Luke concerning the birth of Jesus Christ in Bethlehem, as of a good man.

Then the Magi came and brought him gifts, gold and incense and myrrh as King of Ages.

Let us adore Christ with the Magi, who recognized him whom the Virgin bore that he might save our race.

He is the one who saves his people from transgression; behold, we are his people, his glorious inheritance.

Blessed art thou, O Lord Christ; deliver us from temptations, through the prayers of the Virgin, Mary the daughter of the just.

Great is the glory of Mary, above the righteous and just, the mother of Christ the eternal, the rejoicing of Christians.

The One of the Trinity, consubstantial with the Father, she bore him, Mary the blessed maiden.

Guard us from the respect of men, and cast forth their counsel, for the sake of the praise of women, Mary the mother of Light.

Hear the saying of Micheos: he announced boldly concerning the birth of Jesus Christ in Bethlehem of Judea.

We glorify thee in truth, O Mother of Christ the true king, hope of those who fall, advocate of the righteous.

Lo, John testified: "Behold, a woman clothed with the sun and the moon, and the stars of heaven were a crown on her head."

The true sun is Jesus Christ, and the woman is Mary the Virgin, and the moon is John the precursor, and the stars the twelve apostles.

Hail, Mary the Virgin; hail, temple of heaven; hail, mother of the Word, Jesus the Lamb of God.

To every soul give refreshment in the bosom of our just fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for the sake of Mary the Virgin.

O Saviour, remember, I am the dust-like Nicodemus; purge me, O lover of men, with the rest of Christians. Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls.

title: The Thursday Theotokia (Tone Batos)
text:
I. The bush which Moses saw in the desert was filled with fire, but its foliage was not consumed. It was a type of Mary the pure virgin in whom the Word of the Father came and took flesh. The fire of his Deity did not consume the Virgin's womb, and after she bare him she remained still a virgin. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

II. The praise of all virgins is Mary the Mother of God; on her account passed away the ancient transgression, which came upon our race through disobedience, which was in the woman who ate of the fruit of the tree. On account of Eve the gate of Paradise was closed: on account of Mary the Virgin it was opened again. We have approached the tree of life that we might eat thereof, that is the body of God and his true blood. Let us praise our Saviour, the good Lover of men, for he had pity on us; he came and saved us. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

III. What is the mind or speech or hearing that is capable of the unutterable description of thy love for man, O God? The one Word itself begotten before the ages in Divine manner without body of the one Father. And this same One again was begotten in bodily form without change or detriment through his mother. And still after she bare him her virginity did not cease; by this it was evident that she was mother of God. O depth of love and wisdom of God, that the womb which had been sentenced to bear children in sorrow became a fount of immortality: it bare for us Emmanuel without seed of man, and removed destruction from our race. Let us sing and say to him, Glory to thee, incomprehensible, good Lover of man, Saviour of our souls, who came and saved us. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

IV. The honour of the conception of the virgin womb and of the Mother of God without seed did the angel testify, whom Joseph saw. In this wise he spoke to him: "That which she shall conceive is of the Holy Spirit." That is the Word of the Father: he came and took flesh in her, without change of substance she conceived him; he added this and said: "She shall conceive a son, his name shall be called Emmanuel, which is interpreted 'God with us'." And again: "Thou shalt call his name Jesus, for he shall save his people from their transgressions." How are we his people? he saved us by his strength, he put away our sins, that we might know him with certainty. For he is truly God, he became man without essential change; glory is due to him henceforth for ever. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

V. O the child-bearing of Deity and of continuing the same, Mary the Mother of God who continues always a virgin. For these are with her in one place together, undefiled virginity and true motherhood. For indeed there was no marriage for that conception, nor yet did the conception destroy her virginity. For he who was begotten as God, passionless from the Father, was begotten again as to the flesh, passionless from the Virgin. There is one out of two, Deity and humanity; thus the Magi worshipped him and silently adored him. They brought him incense as God and gold as king, and myrrh signifying his death and coming to life. These things he did for us in his good will, himself the one good Lover of men, the Saviour of our souls; who came and saved us. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

VI. O great miracle that there was taken a rib from the side of Adam, that it might be made a woman. All the mass of manhood she gave in completeness to God the Creator and the Word of the Father. He took flesh from her without essential change. She conceived him as man, his name was called Emmanuel. Her let us supplicate as always Mother of God, that she intercede for us before her beloved son. For very greatly is she sanctified with all the saints, the patriarchs, for she bare to them him whom they contemplated. And the prophets in like manner, him of whom they prophesied in many ways and a multitude of figures, that he had mercy and saved us. And the Apostles as well, that she is the one who gave birth to him who was proclaimed in all the world. The athlete martyrs that he came of her, he who is the true athlete, our Lord Jesus Christ. Let us glorify the greatness of his perfect manhood, and his infinite wisdom to attain his great mercy. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

VII. The Lord sware to David in Ruth and confirmed it, that of the fruit of thy body will I place upon thy throne. O thou whom the Just One consoled, because thereof Christ was born in the flesh, and encircled thee completely. To find a dwelling for the Lord God the Word, and this he carried out with great watching. And forthwith he cried, and in the Holy Spirit said: "We have heard it in Ephrata", for that is Bethlehem. Emmanuel our God made the place suitable that he should be born there in flesh, according to that saving word. As again said Micheos the prophet: "Thou, O Bethlehem, in the land of Ephrata, art not least amongst the princes of Juda, for from thee shall a prince come, who shall rule my people Israel." What is this agreement of the prophets who prophesied with one spirit about the birth of Christ? This is the glory due to him and his good Father and the Holy Spirit henceforth for ever. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

VIII. The One from the Trinity, consubstantial with the Father, saw our weakness and our dire servitude. He bent the heaven of heavens, he took for mother the Virgin, he became man in her except only as regards sin. He was born in Bethlehem according to the saying of the prophets, he planned to save us for we are his people. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

IX. I saw a wonder appearing in heaven, behold a woman clothed with the sun; there was also the moon under her feet. There were twelve stars, they were a crown upon her head; she was pregnant, she suffered travail, she cried out and gave birth. That was Mary, the new heaven upon earth; it was the sun of righteousness who came to us through her. The sun which clothed her is our Lord Jesus Christ, and the moon which was beneath her feet is John the precursor. And the twelve stars which were a crown upon her head were the twelve Apostles, they surround her and glorify her. Wherefore all nations glorify the Virgin, for she bare God to us in her perfect virginity. He who dwelt with us was God; he came and became Son of Man, but he is truly God: he came and saved us.

title: The Thursday Theotokia — Crown
text: God the unseen in the generations of all ages; Moses upon the mountain came to see his glory. For he saw the bush that was full of fire, but its foliage did not burn, nor did its leaves perish. The fire shone out in the unconsumed bush, for God was therein, and he said to the prophet: "O Moses, Moses, Moses, serve me; I am the god of thy fathers, there is none other than me. Take off thy shoes from thy feet, for the ground whereon thou standest is holy, O Prophet." Consider the bush which is full of fire, yet its foliage is not burned nor its leaves destroyed. It was a type of Mary the pure virgin, the Word of the Father came and took flesh in her. Wherefore we sing in chorus with the virgin John, "Holy is this spouse adorned for the lamb." We pray thee be mindful, O faithful mediator, before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he take away our sins.

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Friday (Tone Batos)
text:
Truly I give glory to the great chief, that is the saving name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they might escape the edge of the sword.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they might quench the might of fire.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they might stop the mouths of lions.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they should cast out demons.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they should heal every disease.

Our Lord Jesus Christ gave signs to his servants who fear him, that they should be lords over their enemies.

That was the mighty name of our Lord Jesus Christ and his life-giving cross whereon he was suspended.

O blessed is the man who casts aside the pollution of this life, and cares for things above, those things which affect the soul.

And that he bear his cross day by day, and that he join his mind and heart to the saving name of Christ.

May our heart be glad, may our tongue rejoice, whenever we consider the saving name of Christ.

Wherefore let us glorify our Lord Jesus Christ, and his good Father, and the Holy Spirit. Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls.

title: Alternative Psali for Friday
text:
I who am a creature of dust, I speak the glory of the virgin: "Blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed the fruit of thy womb."

Every creature, O beloved, glorifies thee many times, O Mary, mother of God, pure virgin.

For thou art the Mother of God, the mother of the true light; for he, the sun of righteousness, came to us through her.

David the king of old said, "The true queen has given birth, there is healing in his wings," for he is the Creator.

Wherefore we also rejoice and exalt him in hymns; he has taken what is ours, he has given to us what is his.

The seven hosts, O holy one, glorify thee, O new heaven, for blessed art thou above heaven and holy above the earth.

Lo, we glorify thee always, we glorify thee who art full of glory, for thou art above everything who is able to relate thy glory.

This is the city of the king, Sion is the mother of Christ, for it is that which is like thee, O Mary, mother of the Word.

Similarly the city of Jerusalem is Mary the Mother of God, for he who is above the cherubim came and took flesh of her.

Wisdom is the Lord's, he has loved the pure one; blessed art thou, O Mary, mother of our Lord Jesus Christ.

All nations and kings glorify the bride Mary, for the Ancient of Days came from thy womb.

Mary, the daughter of the holy ones, conceived Christ after the flesh; he gave to us his Holy Spirit and he took our flesh.

The prophets and all the just spoke of thee, O Queen, for the multitude of women uplift praise and exalt thee above all persons.

Thou art uplifted, O pure one, O thou full of praise; thou art the gladness of virgins, O Mary, the Mother of God.

Great is the glory of the Mother of God, the Mother of Christ the unconfined; he gave pasture to our fathers, she gave milk within her.

The virgin is always the flower of sweet smell, the fountain of life of every creature; pray to Christ on account of our sins.

Rejoice, O new heaven, Mary the healing of our diseases; for the fruit of thy womb has come and saved the world.

Thou art exalted over the cherubim, O faithful advocate, holy above the seraphim, Mary the saving of our father Adam.

We glorify thee with gladness, O all-holy Virgin, for thou didst bear the unconfined, the unlimited Christ.

Behold we say, Hail to thee, O thou cloud covering Christ, for thou art the spiritual knowledge which did console Christians.

He who made the heaven of heavens took flesh in the womb of the holy one, to give light beyond the sun, for thou art the beauty of the dawn.

Hail pure dove, hail mother of the Word, hail mother of the Master, our Saviour the Son of God.

To every soul, O Lord, give them a share and portion in thy kingdom with all thy saints through the intercessions of the Virgin.

O Saviour, remember me, I am the dust-like Nicodemus; place me, who am a sinner, with the fold of Christians. Whenever we sing psalms, let us say with sweetness, O Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on our souls.

title: The Friday Theotokia (Tone Batos)
text:
I. Blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed the fruit of thy womb, O Mary, mother of God and pure virgin. For there came to us through her the sun of righteousness; there was salvation on his wings, for he is the Creator. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

II. Blessed is she above the heavens, honoured above the earth, she is beyond all memory; who is able to speak of her glory? There is none like thee, O Mary the Virgin; the angels glorify thee, the seraphim magnify thee. For he who is above the cherubim came and took flesh in thee, that he might join us to him through his love. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

III. Blessed art thou, O Mary, blessed is thy fruit, O Virgin Mother of God, glory of virginity. He who was before the ages took flesh in thee, the Ancient of Days came from thy womb. He took our flesh, he gave his holy Spirit, he made us one with him through his love. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

IV. A multitude of women give praise; exalted art thou above all persons, thou art the praise of virgins, O Mary, Mother of God. Spiritual city in whom was he that is Most High, who sitteth above upon the chariots of the cherubim. The seraphim glorify him who was placed in thy arms, who gives food to all flesh through his kindness. He bore with us God; thou didst give milk to him, for he is our God and the Saviour of every creature. He is for ever and ever; we praise him, we glorify him, we exalt him. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

V. The Virgin Mary, the Mother of God most wise, the blossom of sweet scent, the holy fountain of eternal life. The fruit of thy womb came and saved the world without anger with us that he might bestow on us his peace. Through his cross and holy resurrection he restored man again to Paradise. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

VI. The Virgin Mary, the holy Mother of God, the faithful advocate of the race of men. Intercede for us before Christ whom thou didst bear, that he vouchsafe to us the purging of our sins. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

VII. The Virgin Mary cried aloud in the temple, "I am the beloved whom God has brought up." For there is no knowledge other than the voice of the angel; he brought good tidings to us of joy coming to us from heaven. He took those things which were ours, he gave to us those which were his; let us sing to him and glorify him, let us exalt him.

title: The Friday Theotokia — Crown
text: I signified thee, O all-holy Virgin, that thou didst bear the Infinite and Incomprehensible at once. Melodies indeed laud thee, O thou adorned with every honour, for thou wast the dwelling of the wisdom of God. Thou wast the spiritual hook catching Christians, teaching them adoration of the life-giving Trinity. Thou art the one bearing the pillar which Moses saw, that is the Son of God; he came and was in thy womb. Thou wast the ark for him who made heaven and earth, thou didst bear him in thy womb for nine months. Thou art she who was entrusted to overshadow the heaven and earth; thou wast to us an opening of the road which leads to heaven. Thou art glorified above the sun, thou art the coming of the dawn, that is a true covering over him in joy and gladness. Judgement was passed on Eve that she should bear in sorrow; thou however didst hear, "Hail, thou full of grace." Thou didst bear to us the king, the Lord of all creation; he came and saved us from our sins, as being good and loving men. Wherefore we sing with Elisabeth thy cousin, "Blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb." We offer also felicitations with Gabriel the angel: "Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee." We pray thee be mindful, O faithful mediator, before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he take away our sins.

title: Psali "Lord Jesus" for Saturday (Tone Batos)
text:
The remembrance of thy holy name has given joy to our souls, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Everything praises thee, those in heaven and in earth, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

For it is thou alone who art worthy of praise, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Just and worthy and entitled to praise and honour, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

All the nations upon earth praise thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Seven times a day do I praise thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Rightly do we praise thee, for we are thy people, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

The beauty of thy holy name is in the mouths of thy saints, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

From dawn to evening daily I will praise thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

In every breath will I honour and praise thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Every fetter of sin cast from our souls, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Every suggestion of the enemy expel from us, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

My every breath praises thee according to the word of the prophet, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Above every dominion thou art the King of Kings, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Praise to thee and thy Father and the Holy Spirit, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Thy name is sweet and blessed in the mouths of thy saints, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

For my mouth shall praise thee and my tongue shall glorify thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Rightly do we praise thee, rightly do we glorify thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

We labour for ever to praise and bless thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Every hymn of praise we uplift to thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

To thee be glory and honour with thanksgiving, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Holy Lord, and holy, holy is God in truth, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Every soul blesses thee, every knee bows to thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

O name full of glory, O name full of praise, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

For ever and ever we praise and bless thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

To thee is praise and glory and honour, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

With praise we praise thee, with glory we glorify thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

As we live we bless thee, as we have being we glorify thee, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Perfect every praise that is put forth in thy holy name, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Make us to pray; we are sinners, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Give us thy true peace; purge away our sins, O Lord Jesus, good Saviour.

Whenever we sing, let us say with sweetness, "O Lord Jesus Christ, be merciful to our souls."

title: Alternative Psali for Saturday
text:
Come all with earnest desire, let us sing to God the eternal, that is from generation to generation, let us laud him for ever.

Every city and every village and those who are upon earth, praise God in every language, for thine is the power and might.

For he sent forth his people and found our condition in his mercy; he took flesh in the virgin through the abundance of his mercy.

David the psalmist spoke, he said words of praise: "Place me in the holy mountain, Lord, bring me to the gates of Sion."

That is the Virgin, the holy and pure, Mary, Mother of God, the true Queen.

Duly with honour we greet her; as a spotless dwelling the Holy Spirit came upon her.

Behold through her fruit was salvation revealed to the race; God did reconcile it again through his goodness.

O root of David, for thou art the race which didst conceive for us the beloved, our Saviour Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ, the only-begotten of the Father, we believe thee without doubt our true God.

For thou art the wise one, O Mary, Mother of God; thou hast become the new heaven upon earth, O mother of God.

Moreover by thy purity thou didst bear him according to prophecy, without seed, spotless, nor marriage, nor intercourse.

Mary, daughter of the holy ones, tabernacle of whom it was said, it is the Holy of Holies, with the ark and the vessel.

The tables of the law, it is thy witness, O virgin; they pointed to the ladder which Jacob saw.

Properly the orthodox call thee the Mother of God; stand by me, O virgin, in friendly way and potently.

Behold, the Lord has come forth from thy womb; he has become our guardian, O thou perfect one.

Again we praise thee: Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee, for thou hast found grace.

The mouths of writers and wise men speak of the glory of Mary; in praises do they exalt her with many honours.

Rightly we also rejoice on account of the beloved mother in a prophetic utterance, to cry aloud with king David.

"Arise, O Lord, before us, thou and the ark." O rod of wood, Mary the pure dove.

Surely art thou blessed, O spiritual table, who didst heal our infirmities and quicken our souls.

O Lord God most merciful, help us, O Lover of man, that we may say with Elisabeth, "Blessed art thou amongst women."

"Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee," with Gabriel, the messenger of good tidings, the angel of the world.

O Saviour of thy people, have pity on those who are sick, heal them; those who are wandering, recall; to those who sleep, O Lord, give rest.

O Lord Jesus Christ, be mindful of me, the least, for the sake of thy virgin mother, and enrol me with thy people. Whenever we sing, let us say with sweetness, "O Lord Jesus Christ, be merciful to our souls."

title: The Saturday Theotokia (Tone Batos)
text:
I. The sinless, pure, and in every way holy one, who bare to us God, and he was placed in her arms. Let all creation rejoice with me; let it cry aloud and say: "Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee." Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

II. We praise thy greatness, O pure virgin; we give greetings with Gabriel the angel. For through thy fruit has power come to our race; God has again reconciled us through his goodness. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

III. As a spotless dwelling did the Holy Spirit come upon thee, and the power of the Most High overshadowed thee, O Mary. For thou didst conceive the true Word, the Son of the Father, who endures for ever; he came and saved us from our sins. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

IV. For thou art of the race and root of David; thou didst conceive for us after the flesh our Saviour Jesus Christ. The only-begotten of the Father before all ages; he emptied himself and took the form of a servant in her for our salvation. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

V. Thou wast the second heaven upon earth, O Mother of God, for the sun of righteousness came to us from thee. Thou didst conceive him according to prophecy, without spot or stain, as Creator and Word of the Father. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

VI. Tabernacle to whom referred the "Holy of holies", wherein was the ark; it was covered with gold on every side. Therein were the tables of the law and the vessel of gold that was full of manna. It was a type of the Son of God; he came and was in Mary the spotless virgin, he took flesh from her. She introduced him into the world, in a unity indivisible; but he is the King of Glory, he came and saved us. Paradise is full of joy that he the Lamb, the Word, the Son of the Father enduring for ever, came and cleansed us from our sins. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

VII. It meant thee, that thou art the mother of God, the true king: after thou didst conceive him thou didst remain still a virgin in a miraculous manner. Emmanuel whom thou didst bear, wherefore he preserved thee; thou art unspotted, and thy virginity is holy. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

VIII. Thou art like the ladder which Jacob saw reaching up to heaven; the Lord was seated at the top. Hail to thee from us, O thou who didst hold the unconfined in thy virgin womb, and contain him on every side. Be to us an advocate before God our Saviour, who took flesh in thee for our salvation. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

IX. Behold, the Lord has come by thee, O thou perfect one, to save the world which he made on account of his great mercy. We sing to him and praise him, we exalt him as good and a Lover of man. Have mercy on us after thy great mercy. Hail thou full of grace, hail thou who hast found grace, hail thou who didst conceive Christ, the Lord is with thee.

title: The Saturday Theotokia — Crown
text: Hail full of grace, virgin undefiled, chosen completeness of all the world. Lamp inextinguishable, honour of virginity, indestructible temple, and rod of the faith. Implore him whom thou didst bear, our good Saviour, that he take these troubles from us, that he give us his peace. Hail thou full of grace, pure candlestick, who didst bear the lamp, the fire of Deity. Hail saving hope of all the world, on thy account set free from the curse of Eve. On thy account again the dwelling of the Holy Spirit, who came upon thee and sanctified thee. Hail thou whom Gabriel saluted, "Hail, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee." For the good will of the Father was in thy child-bearing, the advent of the son was in thy womb. The Holy Spirit filled with all love thy soul and body, O Mary, mother of God. Wherefore we rejoice with a spiritual joy and prophetic, we cry out with King David. For he arose, the Lord, before thee, thou art the ark; it is thy holy place which is compared to thee, O Mary. We pray thee be mindful, O faithful mediator, before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he take away our sins.

title: The Saturday Theotokia — Crown (Second)
text: Hail thou full of grace, the spotless Virgin, the tabernacle not made by hands, the treasury of Deity. Hail pure dove who didst bring good tidings to us of the peace of God, who didst come down to men. Hail mother of him who became man in his calling us to him and the good will of his Father and the Holy Spirit. Hail vessel of gold that was filled with manna, and rod of wood of fir-wood wherewith Moses struck the rock. Hail thou full of grace, O spiritual table giving life to every creature that eats thereof. Hail unspotted accomplishment of deity, which is for the nourishment of every creature who drinks thereof. I have longed with great desire for the power of the tongue, that I may relate the honour of this virgin and her praise also. That is our joy, and hope, and confidence in the advent of our God and Lord Jesus Christ. We exalt her in a worthy way with Elisabeth her cousin, "Blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed the fruit of thy womb." We give thee salutations with Gabriel the angel, "Hail, thou greatly favoured, the Lord is with thee." We pray thee be mindful, O faithful mediator, before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he take away our sins.
